unit.reading: Initium verborum Esdrae priusquam assumeretur: et dixi, Domine, qui inhabitas saeculum, cuius oculi elevati in superna et aëre,
The beginning of the words of Ezra, before he was taken up. And I said: O Lord, who inhabitest eternity, whose eyes are exalted toward the heights and the air,
et cuius thronus inaestimabilis, et gloria incomprehensibilis, cui astat exercitus angelorum cum tremore,
and whose throne is beyond estimation, and whose glory is incomprehensible, before whom the host of angels stands with trembling,
quorum servatio in vento et igni convertitur; cuius verbum verum, et dicta perseverantia;
whose service is turned into wind and fire; whose word is true, and whose sayings endure;
cuius iussio fortis, et dispositio terribilis; cuius aspectus arefacit abyssos, et indignatio tabescere facit montes, et veritas testificatur:
whose command is strong, and whose ordinance is fearful; whose look drieth up the depths, and whose indignation maketh the mountains to melt, and whose truth beareth witness:
exaudi orationem servi tui, et auribus percipe precationem figmenti tui.
hearken unto the prayer of thy servant, and give ear to the supplication of thy creature.
Dum enim vivo, loquar, et dum sapio, respondebo.
For while I live I will speak, and while I have understanding I will answer.
Nec respicias populi tui delicta, sed qui tibi in veritate serviunt.
O look not upon the sins of thy people, but on those who serve thee in truth.
Nec intendas impia gentium studia, sed qui tua testimonia cum doloribus custodierunt.
Regard not the impious endeavors of the heathen, but of those who have kept thy testimonies with afflictions.
Nec cogites qui in conspectu tuo false conversati sunt, sed memorare qui ex voluntate tua timorem cognoverunt.
Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee, but remember those who according to thy will have acknowledged thy fear.
Neque volueris perdere qui pecudum mores habuerunt, sed respicias eos qui legem tuam splendide docuerunt.
Desire not to destroy those that have lived like beasts, but look upon those who have clearly taught thy law.
Nec indigneris eis qui bestiis peiores iudicati sunt, sed diligas eos qui semper in tua iustitia et gloria confidunt.
Take not indignation at those who are deemed worse than beasts, but love those who always put their trust in thy righteousness and glory.
Quoniam nos et patres nostri talibus languoribus morimur; tu autem propter nos peccatores misericors vocaberis.
For we and our fathers have languished through such diseases; but because of us sinners thou shalt be called merciful.
Si enim desideraveris nobis misereri, tunc misericors vocaberis, nobis non habentibus opera iustitiae.
For if thou hast a desire to have mercy upon us, then shalt thou be called merciful, unto us, namely, who have no works of righteousness.
Iusti enim, quibus sunt opera multa reposita, ex propriis operibus recipient mercedem.
For the righteous, who have many works laid up with thee, shall out of their own deeds receive reward.
Quid enim est homo, ut ei indigneris? vel genus corruptibile, ut ita amariceris de eo?
For what is man, that thou shouldest take displeasure at him? or what is a corruptible race, that thou shouldest be so bitter toward it?
In veritate enim nemo est de genitis qui non impie fecerit, et de confitentibus qui non deliquerit.
For in truth there is none among those born who hath not done wickedly, and among those who confess thee none who hath not transgressed.
In hoc enim praedicabitur iustitia tua et bonitas tua, Domine, cum misertus fueris his qui non habent substantiam bonorum operum.
For in this thy righteousness and thy goodness shall be declared, O Lord, when thou art merciful unto those who have no substance of good works.
